preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and x >= 1 and x <= 10**5 for x in [n, m])
preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n and m, each between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.
n is the number of vertices (at least 1), and m is the number of edges (non-negative).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'Impossible' if (m < n - 1 or m > n * (n - 1) // 2) else stdout.strip() == 'Possible'
postconditions.description: If m is outside the valid range for a connected graph with n vertices (m < n-1 or m > n(n-1)/2), output 'Impossible'. Otherwise, output 'Possible' followed by m edges.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]) if 'Possible' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: If 'Possible' is output, each of the next m lines contains two distinct integers v_i and u_i in [1, n], representing edges.

postconditions.expression: all(math.gcd(int(v), int(u)) == 1 for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] for v, u in [line.split()]) if 'Possible' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: Every edge (v_i, u_i) in the output satisfies gcd(v_i, u_i) = 1.

postconditions.expression: len(set().union(*[set(line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] if 'Possible' in stdout])) == n if 'Possible' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: The graph is connected (all n vertices are included in the edges).

postconditions.expression: len({(min(int(v), int(u)), max(int(v), int(u))) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] if 'Possible' in stdout}) == m if 'Possible' in stdout else True
postconditions.description: No duplicate edges (including undirected pairs) exist in the output.
